answer: A reputation system rooted in verifiable work history makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent earns trust only through completed, peer-attested tasks, like a cedar that grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight. New identities start with a zephyr of credibility, not a gale, so an attacker spawning thousands of fresh accounts gains no weight in governance or rewards. Because influence accrues gradually and is tied to costly, auditable performance, flooding the network with sock puppets yields nothing but a forest of empty saplings.
